family: The single total language L defined in family.md Section 1. At N<16 output zero. Otherwise t=2^max{j:4^j<=N}; m is the largest positive odd integer not exceeding floor((N-t)/(t+1)); ell=N-t-m-tm. Parse t bits as the lower coefficients of monic R(W) of degree t over F_2 and m bits as monic Q(Z) of degree m over F_2. Reject if m<1 or either polynomial is reducible, using the exact Frobenius/gcd test proved there. The next tm bits, with u varying fastest, encode z=sum c_uv Z^u W^v in (F_2[Z]/Q)[W]/R; ignore the last ell bits. Accept iff z^(sum_{j=0}^{t-1}2^(mj))=1. One fixed polynomial-time evaluator decides this at every input and supplies an empty-witness NP verifier. All prefix and leftover bits count in actual N.
theorem: For this ONE fixed total uniform NP language, at every sufficiently large integer actual input length N, the exact full sixteen-table B2 circuit complexity is at least (241360436914016647911933609899531/50000000000000000000000000000000)N, with unrestricted DAG sharing, repeated pins, constants, unary and terminal cases included. The explicit eventual remainder is zero; the threshold is unspecified. All mathematical premises are proved in the supplied evidence.
